invariants: Cold inspect synthesizes deterministic missing tool/step/turn boundaries without changing stored bytes.
read_from returns only the physical contiguous stored suffix, never in-memory events or synthetic closers.
Cold load truncates incomplete or invalid uncommitted bytes before durable repair; reopening the artifact is idempotent.
Damage followed by a committed turn/end, mismatched identity and future format are refused without changing bytes.
An active open live turn is flushed and refused by load, never cold-repaired.
identity: Requested ID must match the stored header for every physical read. Synthetic tool results preserve call identity and source sequence.
ownership: Cold reads own detached event graphs; live inspect borrows the Session snapshot. This bounded contract does not certify shared preparation reservations or persistence retirement ownership.
ordering: Inspect/read_from leave bytes unchanged. Load scans and truncates to the last valid contiguous record, fsyncs, then appends tool results, step/end and turn/end. Read-back and second load see the same balanced graph.
errors: Invalid from_seq rejects before storage access. A bad row or sequence gap before a later turn/end is committed corruption; an uncommitted tail is recoverable. v1 is already future relative to pinned v0.
cancellation: Synchronous Python filesystem work cannot interleave on one event loop. Cross-process writers and cancellable shared preparation coordination are outside this cold recovery contract; public Agent cancellation remains CON-AGENT-FACTORY.
adaptation: Python 3.8/Win7 uses JSONL without Zstandard. Seven exact TS/Python observations run the real upstream JSONL service and local backend; 164 unmodified upstream assertions are a source baseline, not 164 Python parity claims.

rc1_review.scope: Current finite executable provider/consumer corpora, original-browser and extracted observations in the single full receipt. Historical alpha evidence remains historical; no inventory-wide parity, arbitrary ABI/history, paid-provider or Win7 certification.
